clue.text: This guy on Friends has crowd going wild outside

indicators.note: the crowd letters sit outside, around the Friends character
running wild suggests the letters of crowd lose their order and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: Ross Geller is one of the six main characters in the sitcom Friends

explanation.surface: A TV character from Friends turns up and the crowd goes wild around him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'This': the very puzzle the solver is working on. Ross Geller is a character in the sitcom Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle refers to itself: the grid being solved is the very thing called this.

clue.text: Engineer's drawing share of profits on tour?

parts.note: a cut is someone's share of the takings
a band or team on tour is away from home

explanation.surface: A band on tour wonders what share of the profits it will see.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutaway is a technical illustration with part of the casing removed to show the inner workings.

clue.text: Lying a little on top of drinking too much?

definitions.text: Lying a little on top of

parts.note: over- as a prefix means excessively, as in overdo
lapping is drinking as a cat does, lapping up

explanation.surface: Someone sprawled half over something after drinking too much: a drunken tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one drunken picture, but 'drinking too much' read cryptically is over-lapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that overlap each cover part of another, partly resting on top of it.

clue.text: Tacky band releasing tape initially finish fifty to flog

indicators.note: letting go of the word tape means dropping it from the strip

parts.note: Sellotape is the British brand name for sticky tape, a tacky band
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A band that's past it ends its run, flogging off its gear for fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sellotape is a British brand of sticky tape; take TAPE off it to leave SELLO, then add the F of finish and the F of fifty. 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog something is to sell it; selling off is getting rid of stock by selling.

clue.text: Composer Carl runs into elsewhere

indicators.note: into says the runs abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: off means away, somewhere else
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A composer called Carl runs off to some other place.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana; the clue also nods to Carl Wilson of the Beach Boys.

clue.text: Peter out catching wave on top of surfboard laughs

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits above the second
catching means the dying word holds the wave inside it

parts.note: to peter out is to die away
a roller is a big breaking wave

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A surfer's ride peters out after catching a wave, to the amusement of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works as a placement signal because this is a down answer: the first part sits above the surfboard's top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Drolleries are comic jokes or pieces of whimsical humour, things that raise a laugh.

clue.text: Some depression to get around

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bout, a spell, of depression, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is a period of low spirits; whole, it means approximately. 'to get' merely links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means approximately or round about, and split in two it names a spell of illness or mood.

clue.text: White guys 2 31, say

parts.note: Pet Sounds, the answer at 31, is an example of an album

indicators.note: the answer to 2, overlapping, tells the two words to share their common letter

parts.note: men are guys

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle: men and a famous record somehow make something white.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBUM and MEN overlap, sharing the M, which is what the answer at 2 tells us to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the clear part of an egg that turns white when cooked, the egg white.

clue.text: Band in Japan starts off ordering burgers in

indicators.note: starts off points to the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A band touring Japan begins by ordering burgers in.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied round a kimono, a band of cloth worn in Japan.

clue.text: Humming works in hit nearly written without Al

parts.note: to tan someone is to thrash them

indicators.note: without says the letters of Al, as written, are dropped from the word nearly

parts.note: taken as written; Al Jardine is a Beach Boy

explanation.surface: Al is left off a nearly written hit song, while someone hums along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' just tells you to take 'nearly' as it is printed. 'Humming' means smelling strongly in British slang; Al Jardine is a Beach Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where hides are cured, notorious for its stink, so it hums.

clue.text: Love 'Til I Die, perhaps definitive single

parts.note: the is the definite article
one is a single

explanation.surface: Reads like a review of the Beach Boys track 'Til I Die' as the definitive single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Til I Die is a Beach Boys song, but here 'Love 'Til I Die' describes the person you will love until death.
explanation.definitionFit: The one is your destined partner, the person you will love until you die.

clue.text: Alternative INRI fable with ordinary fellow in it

definitions.text: Alternative INRI fable with ordinary fellow in it

indicators.note: in it says the two abbreviations go inside the rearranged letters
an alternative version of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A spoof gospel story about an everyday man mistaken for the one under the INRI sign.
explanation.walkthrough: INRI is the inscription placed over Christ on the cross. The whole clue also describes the Monty Python film, an alternative fable about Brian, an ordinary man taken for the Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty Python's 1979 comedy film follows an ordinary man born next door to Jesus who is mistaken for the Messiah.

clue.text: Orchestra parts are successful in 60's UK number one

indicators.note: the orchestra parts the word win, splitting it to sit in the middle

parts.note: to win is to be successful
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Talks of orchestral parts making a hit, the way Brian Wilson's arrangements topped charts in the sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson was the British Prime Minister for most of the 1960s; the clue also hints at Brian Wilson's number one.

clue.text: Cooking on the beach, boy's first to follow American into cold sea?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: into says the American and boy part goes inside cold sea

parts.note: a lake is an inland sea

indicators.note: to follow puts the boy letter after the American abbreviation
first picks the opening letter of boy's

explanation.surface: A boy at a beach barbecue follows an American into the chilly water.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go in after the first letter of the sea word, not at its centre; a lake counts as a sea only loosely, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American seaside party where clams and other food are cooked on the shore.

clue.text: Touring Maine, Carl and Al typically like apple-pie

indicators.note: touring has the letters going round, travelling into a new order

explanation.surface: Beach Boys Carl Wilson and Al Jardine on a tour of Maine, a very American picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder; Carl and Al are the Beach Boys Carl Wilson and Al Jardine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as American as apple pie is quintessentially of the United States, wholesomely national.

clue.text: Puff guy's groovy ability up

parts.note: a puff of air
a guy is a man, with the possessive s
hip means fashionable, groovy

explanation.surface: Someone's cool skill is talked up, puffed as groovy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means in the air: the skill is that of a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmanship is the skill of a pilot, the ability to fly well while up in the sky.

clue.text: Chatter always around piano

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the always word is read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: People always chatter around the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk noisily and at length, or the sharp bark of a small dog.

clue.text: Brother of Carl's content, at the end of the day

indicators.note: at the end of puts the Carl part after the day

parts.note: Fri is the calendar abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Talk of a Beach Boy's brother being content at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' tempts toward the Wilson brothers, but it is a religious brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Silly trumpeter who trundled off during song caught on mic

indicators.note: a microphone picks up sound, so the name is taken as heard

parts.words: trumpeter who trundled off during song
parts.note: Nellie the Elephant packed her trunk and trundled off to the jungle in the children's song

explanation.surface: A daft elephant leaves mid-song, and the moment is caught on a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nellie the Elephant' is a well-known British children's song. 'Silly' here is a noun, a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nelly is a foolish or effeminate person, a silly.

clue.text: Fat American's remarkable LP and BMI

indicators.note: remarkable, read as re-markable, suggests the letters are marked out again in a new order

explanation.surface: An overweight American's long-playing record and body mass index are both noteworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: BMI is body mass index, a measure of obesity; LP is a long-playing record.
explanation.definitionFit: Blimp is American slang for a very overweight person, likened to an airship.

clue.text: God Only Knows blows Filbert away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shrugging phrase for 'I have no idea', also a Beach Boys song
second meaning: Filbert is the setter, so this defeats or bowls over me

explanation.walkthrough: Filbert is the setter, so in the second sense he is 'me': whatever beats him blows him away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a shrug of ignorance, and also literally says something defeats the speaker.

clue.text: Rustic beds mate with 'Wouldn't it be nice to …'

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
'let's' is a suggestion, as is saying wouldn't it be nice to do something; Wouldn't It Be Nice is a Beach Boys song

explanation.surface: A friend suggests a simple country night under the stars, quoting a Beach Boys song.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a crude straw mattress or makeshift bed of the kind found in a rural cottage.

clue.text: In audio, variety of animal parts is satisfying

indicators.note: in audio means heard rather than read, so a word that sounds the same

parts.note: meats are a variety of animal flesh

explanation.surface: A recording praises a satisfying assortment of offal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that meets a need or a standard satisfies it, as in meets requirements.

clue.text: Look? Mike Love crossing street apparently does

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: the Mike and Love letters straddle the street abbreviation, one each side

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Look: Beach Boy Mike Love crosses the street, or so it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Love is the Beach Boys' lead singer, but here he splits into M and O around ST.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone seems to do something, it is apparent that they do, judging by appearances.

clue.text: Band on the radio holds note at the end of Little Bird

indicators.note: holds means the radio band contains the note inside it

parts.note: MW is medium wave, a waveband on a radio dial

indicators.note: at the end of picks the final letter of Little, which is also the note E

explanation.surface: A radio band plays the Beach Boys track Little Bird, holding a note at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' looks like a sound-alike signal but is part of the band: medium wave. The E at the end of Little doubles as the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A mew is a gull, a common seabird, especially the small one.

clue.text: Picking up oddly smelly Scotsman's good vibrations

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the letters so they read upwards
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of smelly

parts.note: braw is Scots for good or fine

explanation.surface: Smelling something odd, a Scotsman still picks up good vibrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives SEL from smelly; add BRAW and 'Picking up' reads SELBRAW upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Warbles are trills, the quavering sounds of song, and a warbling voice vibrates.

clue.text: Doctor Gene Landy ignoring bounds of duty over LA resident

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, here rearranging the letters
ignoring means the named letters are left out of Landy
the bounds of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Dr Eugene Landy, Brian Wilson's controversial therapist, neglects his duties toward a Los Angeles patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Eugene Landy was Brian Wilson's real-life therapist, so 'Doctor' reads as his title, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native or inhabitant of Los Angeles, the city's demonym.

clue.text: Go astray during peak in awful mental state

indicators.note: during places the straying word in the course of the peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
to err is to go astray

explanation.surface: A climber loses their way on a summit and panics.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, an awful frame of mind.

clue.text: Hit band

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a strip worn round the waist

explanation.walkthrough: In a Beach Boys puzzle 'Hit band' looks like praise of the group, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for striking forcefully and a noun for a waist strap.

clue.text: Playing records, 20/20 rehashed these

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two twenties are scores

indicators.note: rehashed means the word these is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Records of play with perfect eyesight rehashed: an eye-test pun.
explanation.walkthrough: 20/20 looks like perfect vision, but it is two twenties, i.e. two scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Score sheets are the forms on which the play in a game or match is recorded.

clue.text: See 9
Firm line taken for depression

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm line is taken on economic depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks, a low point in a ridge.

clue.text: Of bands never making a comeback, a proportion quits

indicators.note: a comeback returns the way it went, so the letters run backwards
a proportion means only a part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Among bands that never reunite, a share give up for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'bandS NEVEr' read backwards. 'quits' is an adjective, as in 'we're quits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits or evens means neither side owes the other anything; the score is level.

clue.text: Record 15 and 22?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Beach Boys' 1966 album
second meaning: the answers at 15 and 22, yap and mew, are noises a dog and cat make

explanation.walkthrough: The two cross-referenced answers are a dog's bark and a cat's cry, so together they are the noises of household animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a celebrated Beach Boys album and literally means noises made by domestic animals.
